messages:
kai: noticing a weird IO scheduler panic on gpu-108 (nvme0) in prod-us-east1, throughput dropped to single-digit MB/s and several GPU jobs stalled :eyes:

kai: example log: `nvme nvme0: I/O 0x7f9d1c: rq=0x0, qid=2, status=-110 (Timeout)`, followed by `blk_mq: io scheduler panic`

anita: can you paste the full dmesg tail and which pods were affected?

kai: pasted dmesg tail below and attached pod names in thread - short list: trainer-job-22, batch-encode-5. dmesg snippet:
```
[ 3124.451234] nvme nvme0: I/O 0x7f9d1c: rq=0x0, status=-110
[ 3124.451236] blk_mq: io scheduler panic: rq depth overflow
[ 3124.451240] nvme nvme0: reset controller
```

marco: hmm, seen similar when ephemeral-cleaner starts concurrent GC + heavy KV cache writes from the runtime. Two quick mitigations: 1) cordon & drain node to stop new starts, 2) throttle the ephemeral-cleaner on that node (or pause)

sre-oncall: cordoned gpu-108 and started drain: `kubectl cordon gpu-108 && kubectl drain gpu-108 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=10m`

infra-bot: alert created: INC-2026, tags: nvme, gpu, io-scheduler. Notifying storage-eng channel.

kai: paused ephemeral-cleaner systemd timer on node: `systemctl stop ephemeral-cleaner.timer` and `systemctl mask ephemeral-cleaner.service` while we observe.

anita: good. can we also temporarily set IO scheduler to mq-deadline for nvme0 to see if it avoids scheduler path? command: `echo mq-deadline > /sys/block/nvme0/queue/scheduler` (test only)

marco: caution: changing scheduler is low-risk for short window. also suggest lowering nvme_max_io_queues and tuning `rq_affinity=0` if we see irq balancing thrash. for a quick test: `echo 0 > /sys/block/nvme0/queue/rq_affinity`

ops-bot: reminder: changing scheduler may affect latency for other tenants. keep in mind SLA windows.

sre-oncall: migrated 2 critical pods off node, drain finished with 0 node-ready pods for GPUs. observed IO drop to baseline after stopper for cleaner.

kai: observed less error spam after mask + drain. spikes still appear on metric nvme_io_wait but 10x lower. continuing to run soak for 30m.

marco: follow-up plan: 1) add a preemptive throttle for ephemeral-cleaner to limit concurrent writers, 2) schedule kernel backport with blocked nvme reset fix to staging (5.15.x backport), 3) tune kube-scheduler to avoid packing heavy-kv jobs on nodes running scrubs

anita: creating a short runbook in ops/infra playbook: steps to cordon/drain, pause cleaner, set scheduler fallback, and signal SRE. linking ticket INC-2026.

kai: thanks folks. will monitor and update ticket. if soak looks good will roll the cleaner throttle cluster-wide tomorrow morning during low-traffic window :thumbsup:

sre-oncall: final note: we should add a prometheus alert for sustained nvme_io_wait > 100ms for more than 2m to catch earlier next time.

kai: ack, setting up alert after postmortem.
